entities.summary:
The Battle of Austerlitz, fought on December 2, 1805, was a pivotal event in European history, showcasing the military genius of Napoleon Bonaparte as he led a French army to a decisive victory over a combined Austrian and Russian force. This battle marked a turning point in the War of the Third Coalition, cementing Napoleon's reputation as a master tactician and securing his control over much of Europe. The battle's outcome had far-reaching consequences, as Napoleon's armies went on to conquer much of Europe, redrawing the continent's map and shaping the course of modern history. 

The Battle of Austerlitz was a masterclass in strategic planning, with Napoleon employing his 'battle of the three wings' tactic to outmaneuver his opponents. He cleverly positioned his forces on the Pratzen Heights, creating a strong center while weakening his flanks. As the Austrian and Russian armies attacked, Napoleon's forces held firm, and then launched a devastating counterattack that shattered their lines. The battle was a crushing defeat for the coalition forces, with over 27,000 casualties. 

The Battle of Austerlitz had a lasting impact on European history, as it marked the beginning of Napoleon's dominance over the continent. His armies went on to conquer much of Europe, and his influence extended into the Americas, Africa, and Asia. The battle also cemented Napoleon's reputation as a military genius, and his legacy continues to be studied by military historians and strategists around the world. 

The Battle of Austerlitz was a defining moment in the career of Napoleon Bonaparte, who would go on to become one of the most famous leaders in history. His victory at Austerlitz solidified his position as Emperor of France and set the stage for his future conquests. The battle's impact can still be felt today, as it continues to shape our understanding of military strategy and the art of war.
